layerReconciliation.residualAssessment: A cross-task closure role is plausible, but incremental value over hard gates and narrower reviewed workflows is unproved.

overlapAndConflictFindings.finding: All three Skill bodies materially repeat global AGENTS rules, so shared hard-standard passes cannot be credited to Skill value.
Agents and Codex copies are byte-equal while CC Switch copies are older and byte-distinct; canonical runtime ownership and consumer convergence remain unresolved.
Two startup-visible entries per logical Skill increase ambiguity without proving beneficial redundancy or independent loading.
Official host mechanisms expose inventory, explicit input, Hook, thread, and compaction controls but do not substitute for semantic intake, routing, or closure judgment.
Reviewed Matt and Superpowers workflows overlap only bounded subflows; neither currently proves a complete replacement for the three control checkpoints.
The current host cannot independently attribute scenario-relevant Skill loading, so live net value and retirement decisions remain inadmissible under the frozen protocol.
Automatic compression quality, handoff loader delivery, receiver recovery, and cross-host adherence remain outside current evidence.

Official host capability availability is not semantic task quality or automatic continuity.
Reviewed external workflow metadata is not execution admission or live behavior.
Provisional retention is experiment preservation, not permanent product admission.
No repository, Skill, Hook, CC Switch, cleanup, commit, push, or goal-status mutation is authorized by this record.
